cause_quote: The new `<details>` handler called `const blocks = htmlNodesToBlocks(bodyNodes);` without a depth check, reentering the same handler for each nested `<details>` until the stack could overflow.
user_saw: When an assistant reply contained thousands of nested `<details>` blocks, the Telegram user received a generic failure notice and never saw the reply.
summary: The fix bounds Telegram rich-block parsing and rendering, caps nesting at 15 containers, and preserves deeper text and media URLs as plain text.
reasoning: The parent had a rich-block renderer but no `<details>` mapping, and the introducing diff added both uncapped recursion in `unwrapUnclosed` and recursive rendering of nested details bodies. The later Markdown-inside-details rewrite changed the recursive rendering path and still imposed no bound before rendering, so the overflow was possible from the first version of the feature.
